sub_answers.text: References to advocacy by Gough Whitlam, Don Dunstan and Lionel Murphy preceded the removal of any reference to a “White Australia” policy from the party platform in 1967 and the insertion of explicit support for a vigorous and expanding immigration programme and multiculturalism into the Australian Labor Party platform [d48473623s5p0]. The Whitlam government introduced national reforms in multiculturalism and immigration, including the Racial Discrimination Act 1975, which became part of the party’s policy legacy [d48473623s5p0]. Later Labor governments and conference platforms continued to enshrine multiculturalism and commitments to remove barriers to migrants’ participation and to oppose racism, reflected in the ALP National Platform language cited from the 2023 conference [d48473623s5p0].

sub_answers.text: On 16 April 1926 a memorandum was issued to all Gauleiter insisting on pre-approval by Munich of all pamphlets issued by local Party organizations [d72269826s8p0]. On 22 May 1926 Hitler convened a national membership meeting in Munich that approved sweeping changes to the Party bylaws that confirmed his leadership and made him superior to the executive committee, answerable only to the general meeting, and gave him final discretion over expulsions and local branches [d72269826s8p0]. Hitler instituted the Uschla (internal Investigation and Settlement Committee) whose chairman was named by him, and issued new directives for Gaue on 1 July 1926 restricting smaller study-group combinations of Gaue and centralizing authority [d72269826s8p0]. A Party Congress held in Weimar on 3–4 July 1926 reinforced these organizational and disciplinary changes and reserved final programmatic, administrative and organizational decision-making power to Hitler [d72269826s8p0].

sub_answers.text: He first became a member of the German Bundestag in the 2017 elections representing the Delmenhorst – Wesermarsch – Oldenburg-Land district [d21081409s3p0]. Within his parliamentary group he chaired the Bundestag group of FDP parliamentarians from Lower Saxony, Hamburg and Schleswig-Holstein [d21081409s3p0]. He served as one of six deputy chairpersons of the FDP parliamentary group where he oversaw the group's activities on finance and budget policy [d21081409s3p0]. In December 2021 he was elected leader of the FDP parliamentary group in the Bundestag and was re-elected in 2023 by 93 percent of his parliamentary group's members [d21081409s3p0]. He announced his candidacy for the party chairmanship in mid‑March 2025 and was elected at a federal party convention on 16 May 2025 [d21081409s3p0].

sub_answers.text: Four criminal indictments were filed against Donald Trump in 2023—two state (New York and Georgia) and two federal (Florida and the District of Columbia), and he pleaded not guilty to all charges [d73425097s0p0]. The New York case resulted in a conviction while the Georgia charges were dropped and the two federal cases were dismissed after his 2024 election and related Justice Department developments [d73425097s0p0]. The Supreme Court ruled on July 1, 2024, that Trump had presidential immunity for official acts but not for unofficial acts, affecting the scope of prosecutions [d73425097s0p0]. Yulia Tymoshenko was arrested on 13 February 2001 and charged with forging customs documents and smuggling gas from 1997, and Russian prosecutors later opened and then dropped separate bribery charges by December 2005 [d1246843s6p0].

sub_answers.text: Supreme Court ruled on July 1, 2024, that Donald Trump has immunity for acts he committed as president that were official acts but does not have immunity for unofficial acts, creating judicial limits on which actions could be prosecuted [d73425097s0p0]. The Supreme Court separately reversed all state ballot disqualifications and noted that neither the indictments nor resulting convictions would have disqualified his 2024 presidential candidacy [d73425097s0p0]. Justice Department policy and his 2024 election led to dismissal of the federal cases after his inauguration, and the Deputy Attorney General later reported that over 200 Justice Department employees who worked on the investigations had departed [d73425097s0p0].
